ROUTED TO /failure-autopsy by governance cycle governance-20260909 wave 3 (user decision; this flag is the autopsy target, and GFLAG-0195 was resolved pointing here). V3-EXQ-900 (v3_exq_900_sd024_da_cluster_allocation_representational_functional_20260808T103846Z_v3) is a reviewed, non-degenerate, claim-tagged evidence PASS whose own label asserts more than its criteria test. Its combination rule is 'PASS iff C1 AND C2 AND C4', and ALL THREE load-bearing criteria are representational or absence-based: C1 is Spearman rho(dopamine_signal, cluster_size)=0.5327, C2 is rho(cluster_size, density_reader)=0.5166, and C4 is a negative existential (0 cluster allocations across 1403 live harm calls). NOTHING in the rule tests the FUNCTIONAL half of 'da_cluster_allocation_representational_AND_functional'. The one functional discriminator the run does record is FLAT and ungated: mean_benefit_magnitude_across_cluster_sizes_ge2 = 0.5577261900901794 versus mean_benefit_magnitude_across_cluster_size_1 = 0.5582475601224338, a difference of about 0.09 percent, sitting in the pooled block with no criterion attached. Second finding: the readiness floor R3 pooled_live_expansion_events cleared by exactly ONE event (measured 6.0, threshold N_EXPANSION_MIN=5), and mean_cluster_size is 1.3158 with max 8, so the entire cluster-expansion arm rests on 6 events. What the skim CLEARS, so the autopsy need not re-derive it: the thresholds are pre-registered and explicitly NOT derived from this run's statistics (RHO_LIVE_MIN=0.30, cleared by ~1.7x on both correlations, attainable in either direction); C4 is well powered; non_degenerate: true comes from a real input-spread check on cluster_size and density, not from a count floor. THE ASK: adjudicate whether the flat benefit-magnitude readout falsifies, qualifies, or is simply out of scope for SD-024's functional clause, and whether a 6-event expansion arm can carry it. Until that is answered SD-024 stays candidate and is NOT promoted despite reading confirmed_established at experimental_confidence 0.704 with zero conflicting runs. SEPARATELY, and independent of the above: V3-EXQ-795, the second run cited in support of SD-024, is a DIAGNOSTIC PASS with NO confirmed failure_autopsy artifact (verified 2026-09-09 via check_autopsy_coverage.py), so under the Step 1.5a rule it cannot count toward any promotion; it is also tagged SD-025, which inherits the same problem.

CROSS-CUTTING ATTRIBUTION GAP -- recorded once by governance cycle governance-20260909 wave 3 (user decision) as the single owner of a defect that GFLAG-0193, GFLAG-0191 and GFLAG-0202 each describe one instance of. Those three flags are DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN pointing here rather than resolved, because the underlying defect is unfixed. THE SHAPE: a diagnostic experiment correctly carries claim_ids: [] (the deliberate convention that stops a diagnostic weighting a claim), the run then PASSes cleanly and is confirmed and reviewed, and the claim it actually validates is left reading as evidence-free -- so a validated design decision is indistinguishable, to every downstream consumer, from one nobody ever tested. THE THREE INSTANCES: (i) SD-084 is status candidate_substrate_landed with evidence: [] and returns null from claim_evidence.v1.json, while its validating diagnostic V3-EXQ-839 PASSed cleanly (415 vs 0, attributability 4/4 as pre-registered, negative control held, non_degenerate), was CONFIRMED by failure_autopsy_V3-EXQ-839_2026-07-30, and was ratified by governance on 2026-08-10. (ii) MECH-288 sits at experimental_confidence 0.649 from genuine_exp_count 1 (V3-EXQ-757, an action-free synthetic isolation test) while its substrate ran live inside 22 further indexed experiments, none of which names MECH-288 in claim_ids. (iii) V3-EXQ-694 (v3_exq_694_sd061_difficulty_gated_proposal_entropy_readiness) is a reviewed PASS with claim_ids: [], is the ONLY exercise of the SD-061 substrate, and its entropy result (ON-arm first_action_entropy fell -0.0812/-0.0734/-0.0953 on 3/3 seeds while control drift was mixed in sign) is load-bearing for BOTH MECH-343 and MECH-527 -- currently attributable to neither. WHY THIS NEEDS A DECISION RATHER THAN THREE EDITS: the honest fix is not to back-tag claim_ids on diagnostics (that would defeat the convention and let diagnostics weight claims, which is the thing the convention exists to prevent). It is a cross-tag mechanism that records 'this diagnostic validated that claim' WITHOUT granting scored credit -- exactly what the ARC-120 and ARC-130 claim_synthesis passes did by hand in 2026-09-07, and what diagnostic_evidence_adjudicated: true marks after the fact. The open question for governance is whether that hand pattern should become a standing, mechanised route, and if so what reads it. Until then every validated-but-untagged claim will keep re-surfacing as a promotion_review flag, one claim at a time, forever.
items.resolution_note: USER-APPROVED DECISION applied 2026-09-10 in REE_assembly c8116c399b (gov-flagbacklog-20260909; user read the docket and approved the recommendation). All three named instances verify exactly as stated: SD-084 evidence:[]/claim_evidence.v1.json=null despite V3-EXQ-839 PASS+CONFIRMED+ratified (see GFLAG-0193); MECH-288 experimental_confidence=0.649 from genuine_exp_count=1 while ~22 other runs exercise its substrate untagged (see GFLAG-0191); V3-EXQ-694 is a reviewed PASS with claim_ids=[] and is SD-061's only exercise, load-bearing for both MECH-343 and MECH-527, both absent from claim_evidence.v1.json (see GFLAG-0202). New corroborating finding: V3-EXQ-839's own manifest already carries a bears_on:[SD-084,...] field, but build_experiment_indexes.py never reads any 'bears_on' key (zero grep hits) -- the exact plumbing this flag asks governance to consider already exists in one producer and is inert. The proposed precedent (evidence_direction_per_claim stamped by hand, claim_ids left untouched) is independently confirmed as already-used practice: commits 5a56e04ad6 and d0f11e8e6a (both dated 2026-09-07) did exactly this for ARC-120 and ARC-130. DECISION AS APPLIED: This is the parent governance decision for the whole cluster (per its own text, correctly so). OPTIONS: (a) status quo. (b) back-tag claim_ids on diagnostics -- explicitly rejected in the flag's own reasoning, and independently confirmed here to conflict with the CLAUDE.md claim_ids Accuracy Rule. (c) build a mechanised bears_on/cross-tag reader in build_experiment_indexes.py that surfaces but does not score these attributions -- the field already exists unread on at least one manifest (V3-EXQ-839), and the manual equivalent (evidence_direction_per_claim with claim_ids untouched) is already established governance practice from the 2026-09-07 ARC-120/ARC-130 passes. RECOMMENDATION: (c) -- wiring the indexer to read the already-present bears_on field (or formalising the evidence_direction_per_claim-without-claim_ids pattern) would resolve GFLAG-0191/0193/0202 in one mechanism and prevent this from recurring 'one claim at a time, forever' as the flag itself puts it. Record: evidence/planning/governance_flag_adjudication_20260909.md. RESIDUAL: Cross-cutting flag explicitly raised as a user-decision item by governance-20260909 wave 3. Verified as the correct parent for GFLAG-0191/0193/0202; all facts check out and one new supporting fact (the dormant bears_on field) was found during this adjudication.

items.summary: CORRECTS the GFLAG-0244 resolution note, and records a MEASURED residual the 0244 framing missed. GFLAG-0244's producer fix is sound and stands (ree-v3 5181e49613: pack_writer.write_flat_manifest now sets top-level dry_run:true with the _dry_ filename marker). But its resolution note asserted that GFLAG-0117's consumer-side half was still open, with 27 typedir manifests unreachable by the enumerators. THAT IS WRONG and should not be relied on: the three-shape enumerator (flat, typedir, pack) landed 2026-09-07 in generate_pending_review.py and check_dry_run_citations imports it, so all three shapes ARE enumerated. THE REAL RESIDUAL, measured live 2026-09-09 by running the corpus through the live consumer rather than reasoning about it: two dryness checks over the same corpus have DIFFERENT ARMS. sync_v3_results._is_dry_run has THREE -- (1) dry_run field truthy, (2) flat_path.name.startswith('_dry_'), (3) run_id.endswith('_dry'). generate_pending_review._is_dry_run has TWO -- the field, and _DRY_RUN_ID_RE = re.compile(r'_dry_[0-9]{8}T[0-9]{6}Z') which REQUIRES a timestamp. A bare trailing _dry (no timestamp) passes the regex, and a _dry_-PREFIXED filename with a clean run_id is structurally invisible because _is_dry_run(d: dict) never receives the path. CONSEQUENCE: of 41 dry-named manifests carrying no top-level dry_run field, 26 are excluded by the timestamped regex and 15 LEAK PAST EVERY ARM. 14 of the 15 carry an ASSERTING evidence_direction (13 does_not_support, 1 supports) against the claims tagged here. This is why the two checks disagreed in the field: sync kept ALL of them out of claim_evidence.v1.json (verified: 0 of 29 affected run_ids appear there, lookup sanity-checked against the real run ids for the same experiment types), while pending_review and GOV-DRY-1's asserting-stamp sweep did not. NOTHING IS CURRENTLY MIS-SCORED -- latent trap, not active mis-weighting -- but 14 of the affected run_ids are ALREADY IN reviewed_run_ids, i.e. a past session mark-discussed a smoke, which is the failure mode GFLAG-0244 predicted and which has therefore already occurred. THE 15: _dry_v3_exq_918a_sd_residue_valence_bound_validation_20260909T062139Z_v3.json (supports; the filename-prefix case), v3_exq_324b_sd020_harm_surprise_pe_dry.json, and the _dry-suffixed typedir manifests under v3_exq_259, 318, 319, 320, 321, 321a, 322, 322a, 323 (supports), 323a, 324, 325, 325a. ROUTING: the CODE half is chipped as chip-20260909-isdryrun-parity-gap (task_bcfa6431) -- bring generate_pending_review._is_dry_run to arm-parity, which zeroes the leak with no corpus write and is strictly preferable to stamping. The CORPUS half is governance's call and is NOT chipped: if any of the 15 warrants a quarantine stamp, only superseded / non_contributory are safe values, and the 14 reviewed_run_ids entries may want revisiting. NOTE the parity fix must not be read as re-legitimising a filename heuristic AS THE FIX -- GFLAG-0244's point stands that the source is the writer; this is the historic-corpus half, and the two are complementary, not alternatives.

items.summary: PIPELINE / RECORDING-STANDARD DEFECT, corpus-wide (the four named claims are instances this cycle tripped over, not the scope). MEASURED 2026-09-09 across all non-dry flat manifests in evidence/experiments/: of 534 manifests that declare a load-bearing criteria list, 486 (91.0 percent) record ZERO load-bearing criteria carrying BOTH a measured value and a threshold -- not merely some missing, none at all -- and 180 of those 486 are outcome PASS. Only 40 (7.5 percent) are fully re-derivable. Separately, 489 carry no combination_rule at all. CONSEQUENCE, and why this is a governance problem and not a tidiness one: a criterion recorded as passed: true with no measured value and no bar cannot be checked from the manifest, so the /governance Step 2b MANDATORY DRIVER SKIM -- specifically its 2026-08-30 threshold-arithmetic clause, 'given the magnitudes this run actually measured, is the bar attainable in both directions, or does one branch fire BY CONSTRUCTION' -- cannot be discharged by reading the artifact. It requires opening the driver source every time. That is exactly how V3-EXQ-936a's absolute bar, ~7,900x above the maximum attainable effect, was logged clean for three consecutive cycles. This cycle alone the gap forced a driver read three separate times, and each read found something the manifest could not have shown: V3-EXQ-900's PASS label asserts a FUNCTIONAL half that no criterion tests while the one functional discriminator recorded is flat to 0.09 percent (GFLAG-0246); V3-EXQ-642b's C1/C2 read a DV clamped at 1.5 in both arms so the separation is 0.0 by construction (GFLAG-0141, already autopsied); V3-EXQ-231a's C2 is an arithmetic consequence of its C1 under the driver's own linear map, so it cannot fail when C1 passes (GFLAG-0163, MECH-106 demoted on it). None of those three were visible in the manifest. SUGGESTED DIRECTION, not prescribed: this is the same shape as the flat-scalar-readout gap the Experimental Recording Standard v0.2 closed on 2026-09-09 (REE_assembly d2da351f03, ree-v3 f204ee02ce), and the precedent there is instructive in BOTH directions -- that check was deliberately made ADVISORY in every mode, including --strict, precisely because the corpus gap was too large to gate on (802 of 1008 flat manifests lacked the field). A 91 percent gap is larger still, so a blocking gate is not the move; an advisory validate_recording check plus a standard section requiring measured + threshold on every load-bearing criterion, forward-only, is. Whether the 180 already-PASSING manifests get backfilled is a separate and much bigger question that should NOT be assumed.
items.resolution_note: CLOSED by Experimental Recording Standard v0.3 (REE_assembly bc3d93e61a, on origin/master) + the two advisory checks (ree-v3 ef2bcb2b74, on origin/main). (1) Standard sec 3b gains 'Re-derivable criteria': every LOAD-BEARING criterion must record its MEASURED value and its THRESHOLD as separate machine-readable numeric fields (not prose), plus combination_rule when more than one is load-bearing. (2) validate_recording.check_criteria_thresholds (written manifest; verdicts none_rederivable / partial / criteria_unrecorded / combination_rule_only) and validate_experiments.criteria_threshold_lint (AST, on the driver's load-bearing criterion literals), registered as check 'criteria_threshold' and run by default. (3) ADVISORY IN EVERY MODE including --strict and --paths, pinned by contract class CriteriaNeverBlocksUnderStrict -- the flat-scalar-readout precedent, applied for the same reason. (4) Tests: 14 new contracts in ree-v3/tests/contracts/test_criteria_threshold_lint.py plus 3 classes in test_validate_recording.py; full ree-v3 suite green on the hub (5945 passed, 44 skipped, 1 xfailed, exit 0). MEASUREMENT CORRECTION, recorded in the standard's v0.3 GOV-HELDOUT-1 section: this flag's headline figures (534 manifests / 486 at 91.0 percent / 180 PASS / 40 re-derivable / 489 no combination_rule) did NOT reproduce -- sweeping evidence/experiments/ no definition yields a 534 denominator (the widest construction, flat plus pack manifests carrying either criteria or a combination_rule, gives 233). Reproducible figures under a stated predicate: of 983 live flat manifests, 216 carry a load-bearing criteria set and 184 of those (85.2 percent) record NOT ONE criterion carrying both halves, 53 of them outcome PASS; 32 fully re-derivable; 133 of 216 have more than one load-bearing criterion and no combination_rule. THE PHENOMENON IS CONFIRMED and all four named runs are exactly as described -- only the magnitude differs. GOV-HELDOUT-1 run: CAUGHT AN OVER-BROAD RULE TWICE (a literal spelling list flagged 26 criteria across 14 genuinely-compliant manifests; and scoping to load_bearing:true alone exempted the corpus's worst shape, 101 bare name-to-bool maps, by construction). STILL OPEN, DELIBERATELY OUT OF SCOPE AND LEFT TO GOVERNANCE: back-filling the 53 already-PASSING manifests this check flags -- a criterion whose bar turns out unattainable may invalidate the run's VERDICT, not merely its recording, so it needs a governance decision rather than a recording-standard amendment. Recommendation recorded in the standard sec 4: triage those 53 by claim load-bearingness first. No claim status and no evidence_direction was changed by this work.

items.summary: BACK-FILL TRIAGE owed by the GFLAG-0249 fix -- a DECISION for governance, not a recording task, and it currently has no owner (GFLAG-0249 is resolved, so nothing re-derives it; the named claims are the highest-count instances, not the scope). The Experimental Recording Standard v0.3 (REE_assembly bc3d93e61a) now requires every LOAD-BEARING criterion to record its MEASURED value and its THRESHOLD as separate machine-readable numeric fields, and the two checks that enforce it are ADVISORY ONLY (ree-v3 ef2bcb2b74) -- deliberately, since 184 of 216 flat manifests carrying load-bearing criteria record none that is re-derivable (85.2 percent). Advisory enforcement fixes the FORWARD flow and changes nothing about what is already landed. MEASURED 2026-09-09 with the shipped check over 983 live flat manifests: 53 manifests with outcome PASS record NOT ONE load-bearing criterion carrying both a bar and a measured value, spanning 40 distinct claims -- and 35 of those 53 carry evidence_direction: supports, i.e. they are actively supporting a claim on criteria that CANNOT BE RE-CHECKED FROM THE ARTIFACT. THE QUESTION GOVERNANCE MUST DECIDE: this is not merely a recording gap, because a criterion whose bar turns out to be unattainable invalidates the run's VERDICT, not only its documentation. V3-EXQ-936a (MECH-439) is the proven instance -- an absolute bar ~7,900x above the maximum attainable effect, PASS, logged clean for three consecutive governance cycles; its C2 could not have failed. The same shape may sit undetected in any of the other 52. RECOMMENDATION, not a prescription: triage the 53 by claim load-bearingness first rather than back-filling wholesale -- most will be inert (a re-derivable-looking PASS whose bar was in fact attainable), and a handful will be 936a-shaped and need the run's evidence_direction revisited. Reproduce the list with: validate_recording.check_criteria_thresholds over evidence/experiments/*.json, keeping outcome PASS with verdict none_rederivable or partial. NOTE ON THIS FLAG'S PROVENANCE: GFLAG-0249's own headline figures (534 manifests / 486 / 91.0 percent / 180 PASS) did not reproduce under any definition; the figures here are from the shipped check and are reproducible from the predicate stated above. The phenomenon was confirmed exactly as GFLAG-0249 described it; only the magnitude differs.

notes: Append-only. A resolved (or superseded) entry is NEVER deleted -- flip status and set resolved_at + resolution_note, mirroring claims.yaml's own supersession-not-deletion convention, so the trail stays auditable. Raise new entries and resolve existing ones only via scripts/governance_flag.py (raise / resolve subcommands), which commits via scripts/ree_commit.py in the same step -- this file lives under evidence/planning/, one of CLAUDE.md's exposed high-contention files, and a hand-edited whole-file read-modify-write here would silently adopt any other session's uncommitted edit (see CLAUDE.md 'Read-modify-write contamination'). /governance reads open items at the start of every cycle (see .claude/skills/governance/SKILL.md); the read is additive/informational only and never auto-resolves or auto-promotes anything -- governance is interactive and a flag's substance is always the user's call.
